questions.stem: Explain how dynamic programming can be used to solve the Edit Distance problem. Include the key steps and the role of the DP table.
markingGuide: Define the Edit Distance problem and its operations (insertion, deletion, substitution).
Explain the initialization of the DP table with base cases.
Describe filling the table using the recurrence relation.
Discuss how the final value in the table represents the edit distance.
Explain how to trace back to find the sequence of operations.
questions.explanation: Dynamic programming solves the Edit Distance problem by using a table to store the minimum number of operations needed to transform one string into another. The table is initialized with base cases where one string is empty. Each cell is filled using the recurrence relation, considering insertion, deletion, and substitution. The value in the bottom-right cell gives the edit distance, and tracing back through the table reveals the sequence of operations.

questions.stem: Describe the process of reconstructing the Longest Common Subsequence from a completed DP table.
markingGuide: Identify the starting point at the bottom-right corner of the table.
Trace back through the table following the choices made (diagonal, top, or left).
Record characters when moving diagonally, indicating a match.
Stop when reaching the top or left edge of the table.
Explain how the recorded characters form the LCS.
questions.explanation: To reconstruct the LCS, start at the bottom-right corner of the DP table and trace back. Move diagonally when characters match, recording them as part of the LCS. Move up or left when characters don't match, following the path of maximum value. Continue until reaching the table's edge. The recorded characters form the LCS.
